title: Server-Sent Events dashboard on AWS Lambda Web Functions
description: Stream live metrics to many browsers over Server-Sent Events from a zero-dependency Node.js Lambda Web Function, using AWS SAM.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern deploys a real-time metrics dashboard that uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) as an AWS Lambda Web Function. With the Lambda invocation model a function returns one response per invocation and the execution environment is frozen afterwards, so it cannot hold a long-lived HTTP connection per browser. Lambda Web Functions run a persistent HTTP server inside a microVM that keeps serving while connections are open, so the same Node.js code that would run on a container or a VM works here unchanged. The app has no dependencies: it uses http.createServer, fs and path only.

GET /api/events responds with Content-Type text/event-stream and never ends the response. The server keeps every open response in a Set, generates a metrics snapshot every two seconds and writes it to all clients as a data: line. POST /api/metrics accepts any JSON body and broadcasts it immediately to every connected client, which is how a deployment tool or a job could push custom events. GET /api/status returns the current snapshot once, and GET / serves a small Chart.js dashboard that opens an EventSource and plots the stream.

The connection set and the counters (active connections, peak connections, total requests) are per sandbox. Each sandbox handles many concurrent connections; when traffic grows the service adds sandboxes, and a client is only reached by broadcasts from the sandbox holding its connection. That is the right scope for dashboards, progress feeds and notifications from the instance itself. For fan-out that must reach every client regardless of sandbox, publish the events through a shared channel such as DynamoDB Streams or SNS and have each sandbox subscribe.

The template sets Timeout to 900 seconds, the maximum, because an SSE response lasts as long as the request timeout; the browser EventSource reconnects automatically afterwards. A single AWS::Serverless::WebFunction expands into the function, an immutable revision and a public HTTPS endpoint (AuthType ApplicationManaged), and SAM generates the execution role with CloudWatch Logs permissions.
See the GitHub repo for deployment instructions.
See the GitHub repo for detailed testing instructions.
